rationale: Lydia brings deep expertise in developer experience and technical education for complex tooling—skills directly applicable to making robotics software more accessible—while Akshath's work in SLAM, perception, and autonomous systems represents the kind of cutting-edge robotics domain that could benefit from clearer developer tooling and educational content. Both are in San Francisco and work at the intersection of sophisticated software systems and practical engineering, offering complementary perspectives on how to communicate and build for specialized technical audiences.
intro_message: Lydia Hallie, meet Akshath Singhal — you both work on deep technical systems in San Francisco, and Lydia's background scaling developer experience at Vercel and Bun could offer fresh perspective on how robotics and SLAM tooling gets adopted by engineers.
